title: Global and local geometric Frobenius operators
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $q=p^a$, and the finite coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: a prime $\ell\neq p$,
a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$,
a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and
$A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and
$a_X:X\to s$ its structure morphism. Write
$g=g_\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$,
where $\gamma$ is geometric Frobenius, and let $\Phi$ be the $k$-linear
$q$-power scheme Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius].
Let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a strict Weil complex
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex], write $M=\operatorname{For}(K,\varphi)$,
and fix $m\geq1$. Use the derived pullback of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the iterated Weil isomorphism
$\varphi^{[m]}:L(g^m)^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map].

1. The global compact-support Frobenius operator is the composite
$$
 F_{c,K}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:
 R\Gamma_c(X,M)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,M).
$$
Here $R\Gamma_c(X,N)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}N)$ is the coefficient
complex of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with point fiber
functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. To specify the first arrow
without an implicit identification, put $T=Lg^*$ and let
$\tau_{c,N}:R\Gamma_c(X,N)\to R\Gamma_c(X,TN)$ be the compact-support
transport of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Let $c_m:L(g^m)^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}T^mM$ be the canonical
pullback-composition isomorphism of
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Define
$$
 g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}=R\Gamma_c(X,c_m^{-1})\circ
 \tau_{c,T^{m-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{c,TM}\circ\tau_{c,M}:
 R\Gamma_c(X,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,L(g^m)^*M),
$$
where the displayed transport composite has exactly $m$ factors;
for $m=1$ it is $\tau_{c,M}$ and $c_1$ is the identity.
Each transport is an isomorphism by
[lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]. The induced operator on
$H_c^i(X,M)=\mathrm H^i(R\Gamma_c(X,M))$ is $\mathrm H^i(F_{c,K}^{\,m})$
for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, with cohomology functor as in
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].

2. For $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, let $\bar x:s\to X$ be its induced
geometric point for the fixed inclusion $\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$.
By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $L\bar x^*M$ is bounded
constructible of finite Tor amplitude on $s$, so its point fiber is
defined. The stalk coefficient complex is
$$
 K_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*M).
$$
Thus the customary notation $K_{\bar x}=L\bar x^*M$ implicitly uses the
point fiber functor. By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points] this geometric
point satisfies $\Phi^m\circ\bar x=\bar x$. Let
$$
 \rho_{x,m}:K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*L(\Phi^m)^*M)
$$
be the identification obtained by this equality and the canonical
isomorphism $L(\Phi^m\circ\bar x)^*\cong L\bar x^*L(\Phi^m)^*$ of
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Using the specified
comparison $\kappa^{(m)}:L(\Phi^m)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(g^m)^*$ of
[prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], define the stalk transport and local
geometric Frobenius by
$$
 \tau_{x,m}=\operatorname{Fib}_s\bigl(L\bar x^*(\kappa^{(m)}_M)\bigr)
              \circ\rho_{x,m}:
 K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}(L(g^m)^*M)_{\bar x},
 \qquad
 F_{x,m}=\operatorname{Fib}_s\bigl(L\bar x^*(\varphi^{[m]})\bigr)
              \circ\tau_{x,m}:
 K_{\bar x}\longrightarrow K_{\bar x}.
$$
The notation $(L(g^m)^*M)_{\bar x}$ uses the same stalk convention.

The comparison with the compact-support description is recorded in
[lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description]; the dependence of the
local operator on the geometric lift and on the degree of the closed
point below is recorded in [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] and
[lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula]. These are forward pointers, not
inputs to the construction.

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, and let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$.

1. The *$m$-th iterate of the global geometric Frobenius* is
$$
F_{c,K}^{\,m}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$
the composite of the canonical
direct-image identification
with the compact-support
global geometric
Frobenius action constructed in the trace-formula chapter applied to
$\varphi^{[m]}$. It is the
endomorphism of the
compact-support
cohomology $H_c^i(X,K)$ in the finite coefficient stage.
1. For a point $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ with geometric point
$\bar x:\Spec k\to X$ lying over $x$, define the *local
geometric Frobenius*
$$
F_{x,m}:K_{\bar x}\longrightarrow K_{\bar x},
\qquad
F_{x,m}=\varphi^{[m]}_{\bar x}\circ\tau_{x,m},
$$
where $\tau_{x,m}:K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \bigl(Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\bigr)_{\bar x}$ is the canonical stalk
transport and $K_{\bar x}=L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}(K)$ is the
stalk complex of the
derived pullback.

Equivalently, $F_{c,K}^{\,m}=R\Gamma_c(X,\varphi^{[m]})\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$,
where $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ is the compact-support base-change isomorphism
along the automorphism $g_\gamma^m$ ([lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description]).
The dependence of $F_{x,m}$ on the lift $\bar x$ and, through a closed point
below, on the degree is described in [lem-trf-local-frobenius-conjugacy] and
[lem-trf-frobenius-degree-formula]; that the transport $\tau_{x,m}$ is defined
for every point $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ is the fixed-point statement
[thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points].

split_report.summary: Expanded the two finite-coefficient Frobenius constructions using existing nodes only. Added the missing strict-Weil and iterated-map dependencies, replaced the E-only global-operator dependency by the finite-level cohomology transport, specified its iterated composite, and constructed the local transport through the scheme-Frobenius fixed point and the specified scheme/Galois comparison. Made the point fiber functor and the induced cohomology operator explicit. Removed unused direct-image, cohomology-sheaf and standalone universal-homeomorphism citations. No new nodes and no proof steps for this definition. Second reading explicitly inserted the inverse pullback-composition map into the global formula, specified its one-factor boundary case, and cited finite-Tor pullback preservation to type the local point fiber.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q117-9ee2236c1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and wrote no fixes; the full review is in review.md. The delivery is the item only, with no new nodes. Every stmt_dep exists, is unmerged and is cited in the statement. The three forward pointers stay as pointers, and walking the dependencies from the item never leads back to it, so there is no cycle. Sources read: the main-20261015 blueprint and its blueprint_update, Deligne Weil II (1.1.7), (1.1.8), (1.1.13) and (1.1.14) (pp. 150-153), and the two Stacks labels the report cites. No SGA source is used. Clause 1: the transport def and clause 3 of the transport-iso lemma both cover A_{E,n}, and each Lg^*N stays in D^b_c, so all T^jM are legitimate inputs. The types of c_m^{-1} and RGamma_c(phi^[m]) match. For m=1 the operator is exactly the compact-support composite of def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius, done at A instead of E. Using naturality of tau_c and def-trf-iterated-weil-map, I showed that the delivered F^m is the m-th power of F^1, so the name 'm-th iterate' is accurate. It agrees with the blueprint's base change along g^m because exchange maps compose. That identification is left to lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description, which keeps true, non-trivial content, and the target is not weakened. Clause 2: x-bar is the k-point that thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points attaches to x, so Phi^m o x-bar = x-bar holds directly. The report is right that g^m o x-bar != x-bar, and routing through kappa^(m) is necessary, as in Deligne (1.1.14). kappa^(m) has the direction the formula needs, and A satisfies its coefficient hypothesis. x-bar is a section of a separated morphism, hence a closed immersion and separated of finite type, so lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude applies and Fib_s is defined. Every arrow of tau and F_{x,m} type-checks. Edge cases pass: m=1, empty X, the zero complex, n=1, and X_0=Spec F_q with phi=u (both operators equal u^m). No hypothesis is added or dropped. Neither def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius (E only) nor def-tw-frobenius-action duplicates the item. There are no tool_uses.
